results.title: Group matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite group $G$, the group matrix of Dedekind and Frobenius is the $G \times G$ matrix over the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ whose entry at $(g, h)$ is the variable $x_{gh}$.

results.title: Group determinant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite group $G$, the group determinant $\Theta(G)$ is the determinant of the group matrix of $G$, the $G \times G$ matrix over $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ whose entry at $(g, h)$ is the variable $x_{gh}$; it is a polynomial in these variables.

results.title: Frobenius determinant theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $r$ be the number of conjugacy classes of $G$. Then there exist polynomials $p_1, \dots, p_r$ in $\mathbb{C}[x_g : g \in G]$ such that each $p_j$ is irreducible, $p_i$ and $p_j$ are not associated for $i \neq j$, and the group determinant of $G$ equals $\prod_{j=1}^{r} p_j^{\deg p_j}$, where $\deg p_j$ is the total degree of $p_j$.

results.title: Sharply doubly transitive action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An action of a group $G$ on a set $\Omega$ is sharply doubly transitive when for all points $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta \in \Omega$ with $\alpha \ne \beta$ and $\gamma \ne \delta$ there is exactly one $g \in G$ with $g \cdot \alpha = \gamma$ and $g \cdot \beta = \delta$.

results.title: Mazurov's question on sharply 2-transitive groups (Kourovka 11.52)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that every group $G$ acting sharply doubly transitively on a set $\Omega$ with at least two points has a nontrivial abelian normal subgroup.

results.title: A sharply 2-transitive group without nontrivial abelian normal subgroups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The statement of Kourovka Problem 11.52 is false: there is a group $G$ acting sharply doubly transitively on a set $\Omega$ with at least two points such that no nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$ is abelian.

results.title: Twisting character of the free group of rank two
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on $x, y$. For nonzero complex numbers $a, b$, this is the homomorphism $\chi \colon F \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ with $\chi(x) = a$ and $\chi(y) = b$.

results.title: Twisting automorphism of the free group algebra
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be the free group on $x, y$, let $\mathbb{C}F$ be its complex group algebra, and for nonzero complex numbers $a, b$ let $\chi$ be the character of $F$ with $\chi(x) = a$ and $\chi(y) = b$. The map $\vartheta_{a,b}$ sends $\alpha = \sum_{g \in F} c_g\, g \in \mathbb{C}F$ to $\sum_{g \in F} \chi(g)\, c_g\, g$.

part.title: Principal minors of the Fourier matrix

path: Principal minors of the Fourier matrix

results.title: Primitive root of unity data
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a natural number $M$ and a commutative ring $R$, root data of order $M$ in $R$ consists of an element $\zeta \in R$ that is a primitive $M$-th root of unity, together with the condition $M \ge 2$.

results.title: Principal Fourier minor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $S$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. The principal Fourier minor indexed by $S$ is the $S \times S$ matrix over $R$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is $\zeta^{n}$, where $n \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}$ is the representative of the product $ij$ in $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Determinant of a principal Fourier minor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $S$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. The principal Fourier minor determinant of $S$ is the determinant in $R$ of the principal Fourier minor indexed by $S$.

results.title: Entries of a principal Fourier minor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $S$ be a finite subset of $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. For all $i, j \in S$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the principal Fourier minor indexed by $S$ equals $\zeta^{n}$, where $n \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}$ is the representative of $ij$ in $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Determinant of the empty principal Fourier minor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity. The determinant of the principal Fourier minor indexed by the empty subset of $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$ equals $1$.

results.title: Determinant of a singleton principal Fourier minor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M \ge 2$, let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\zeta \in R$ be a primitive $M$-th root of unity, and let $a \in \mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$. The determinant of the principal Fourier minor indexed by $\{a\}$ equals $\zeta^{n}$, where $n \in \{0, \dots, M-1\}$ is the representative of $a^2$ in $\mathbb{Z}/M\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Absolute convergence of Ramanujan's Bell-type series (Entry 4)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every complex number $x$ and every natural number $n$, the series $\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{(j+1)^n x^{j+1}}{j!}$ converges absolutely.

results.title: Ramanujan's generalized Bell function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For complex numbers $a$, $b$, $x$ and a natural number $n$, the generalized Bell function is $F(a, b, x; n) = e^{-x} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(a + b(k + 1))^n x^{k+1}}{k!}$.

results.title: Convergence of the generalized Bell series
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ denote Ramanujan's generalized Bell function. For complex numbers $a$, $b$, $x$ and every natural number $n$, the series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} (a + b(k + 1))^n x^{k+1} / k!$ converges absolutely and its sum is $e^{x} F(a, b, x; n)$.

results.title: Exponential generating function of Ramanujan's Bell-type series (Entry 4)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be Ramanujan's generalized Bell function. For all complex numbers $a$ and $x$, let $f(x, n) = F(0, 1, x; n) = e^{-x} \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{(j+1)^n x^{j+1}}{j!}$ for natural numbers $n$, and set $f(x, -1) = 1$. Then the series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{a^n}{n!} f(x, n-1)$ converges absolutely and its sum is $e^{x(e^a - 1)}$.

results.title: Binomial recurrence for Ramanujan's Bell-type series (Entry 5)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be Ramanujan's generalized Bell function. For every natural number $n$ and every complex number $x$, write $f(x, m) = F(0, 1, x; m)$ for natural numbers $m$, and set $f(x, -1) = 1$. Then $f(x, n) = x \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} f(x, k-1)$.

results.title: Exponential generating function of the generalized Bell function (Entry 9(ii))
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F(a, b, x; n)$ be Ramanujan's generalized Bell function. For all complex numbers $a$, $b$, $x$ and $y$, the series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{y^n}{n!} F(a, b, x; n)$ converges to $x e^{(a+b)y} e^{x(e^{by} - 1)}$.

results.title: Generalized Bell function extended to $n = -1$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $n \ge -1$ and a complex number $x$, $f(n, x) = 1$ if $n = -1$, and otherwise $f(n, x)$ is the generalized Bell function $F(0, 1, x; n) = e^{-x} \sum_{k \ge 0} (k + 1)^n x^{k + 1} / k!$.

results.title: Integrability of the scaled generalized Bell integrand on $(0, 1)$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be the generalized Bell function extended to $n = -1$. For every natural number $m$ and every complex number $x$, the complex-valued function $t \mapsto x f(m - 1, t x)$ of a real variable $t$ is interval integrable on $[0, 1]$ with respect to Lebesgue measure.

results.title: Dominating set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S$ of vertices of a simple graph $G$ dominates $G$ when every vertex of $G$ lies in $S$ or is adjacent to some vertex of $S$.

results.title: Independent dominating set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S$ of vertices of a simple graph $G$ is an independent dominating set of $G$ when no two vertices of $S$ are adjacent and $S$ dominates $G$.

results.title: Domination number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the domination number of $G$ is the least number of elements of a dominating set of $G$.

results.title: Independent domination number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the independent domination number of $G$ is the least number of elements of an independent dominating set of $G$.

results.title: Existence of independent dominating sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every finite graph has an independent dominating set.

results.title: A minimum independent dominating set exists
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set has an independent dominating set whose number of elements equals the independent domination number of $G$.

results.title: Independent dominating sets are at least as large as the independent domination number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set. If $S$ is an independent dominating set of $G$, then the independent domination number of $G$ is at most the number of elements of $S$.

results.title: A minimum dominating set exists
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set has a dominating set whose number of elements equals the domination number of $G$.

results.title: Graph-homomorphism instances
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A graph-homomorphism instance is a quadruple $(n, E, m, F)$ where $n$ is a natural number (the number of source vertices), $E$ is a list of pairs of natural numbers (the source edges), $m$ is a natural number (the number of target vertices) and $F$ is a list of pairs of natural numbers (the target edges).

results.title: Target graph of a graph-homomorphism instance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The target graph of a graph-homomorphism instance $(n, E, m, F)$ is the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $F$. Pairs of $F$ with an endpoint at least $m$ contribute no edge.

results.title: Feasible graph-homomorphism instances
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A graph-homomorphism instance $(n, E, m, F)$ is feasible when there is a map $f : \{0, \dots, n - 1\} \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ such that, for every pair $(u, v)$ in $E$ with $u < n$ and $v < n$, the vertices $f(u)$ and $f(v)$ are adjacent in the target graph of the instance, that is, $f(u) \ne f(v)$ and $(f(u), f(v))$ or $(f(v), f(u))$ belongs to $F$. Pairs of $E$ with an endpoint at least $n$ impose no condition.

results.title: Argmax over an initial segment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the argmax of $f$ over $\{0, \dots, n\}$ is the least $k \le n$ such that $f(j) \le f(k)$ for all $j \le n$.

results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the argmax of $f$ over $\{0, \dots, n\}$ is at most $n$.
